Quest RP refreshed source · supplied 23 October 2026 · 3,845 messages across the main channel and two accessible threads; posting chronology and narrated continuations remain distinct
body:
Pelegia, also recorded as Pin, Pell and Pelagia, is one player character.

A Seeker and civic servant

Pelegia explores the contaminated harpy cave with the Seekers. Despite feeling afraid, Pelegia insists that the corrupted corpse deserves burial while the company investigates. Vessalia offers emotional shelter while Di’Trillio, Minerva and Fenwick give the investigation a shared structure.

Later service includes gathering Mama Tabitha’s ingredients, preparing Papirak’s grave, planning a mausoleum and helping with fundraising. These trusted tasks give Pelegia purpose within Pristinia.

The Larkhollow expeditions

Recorded as Pelagia, Pelegia urges retreat from Hana’s tower when the company is in danger, then returns with Ryvyt to question market residents about the forest. Their differing apparent travel durations remain unexplained.

Meeting the company as Pin

Pin is a player character. In his introduction to the company, he gives his name and stays close to Carmen while meeting unfamiliar companions. The scene places him among the adventurers without establishing a home island.

Care after the fight

In a later encounter he offers healing and acknowledges Carmen’s final shot. This preserves an act of practical support without inventing a complete biography, allegiance or later fate.

Pin and the river’s call

Recorded as Pin, Pelegia joins Fenwick, Ryvyt and Minerva in the search for Selwyn. The Eternal River draws him toward it against his will. Ryvyt holds and pulls him back, yet his body visibly ages seven years. The narrator also records an unusual sense of health and happiness; that sensation does not show the effect is harmless or reversible.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

Bargaining for the people who must come home

Pin tries to negotiate for Selwyn’s body while fighting the shadowy figures, rejecting a demand for his actual arm. He continues seeking a way to take both Selwyn and Minerva back without more killing. When Minerva chooses to remain, he accepts her lock of hair and promises to seek a healer if she does not return.

The roots are released from Selwyn, but a branch remains. No completed journey home, resurrection or restoration of either companion is shown in this scene.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

profile.personality: Pell is frightened in ways the record never mocks and practical in ways fear does not erase. The most important part of Pell’s cave history is moral clarity: a corrupted corpse is still somebody’s child, and danger does not cancel the obligation to recognize a life that existed before the horror. Introduces himself to unfamiliar companions while remaining close to Carmen.
profile.achievements: Pell helps the Seekers explore a cave marked by contamination, crystalline anomalies, malformed harpies, and a dead body whose condition becomes evidence. Staying present long enough to observe, argue for burial, and continue with the company is an achievement of endurance rather than spectacle. Pell gives the unnamed cave dead a last prayer before the collapse. At Papirak’s funeral he describes service as a source of purpose after doubting his usefulness on expeditions. The September ingredient quest also shows him helping examine Bogdan, then receiving treatment for an accidental anaesthetic exposure. The tower expedition shows her choosing retreat when the company is in danger. On the market journey, she and Ryvyt experience different apparent travel durations; no single mechanism is established. Offers healing after a fight and acknowledges Carmen’s final shot. Tries to negotiate Selwyn’s release and accepts Minerva’s lock of hair as an obligation to seek help.
profile.relationships: Vessalia’s attention gives Pell emotional shelter, while Di’Trillio’s technical observations and Minerva and Fenwick’s investigation give the fear a shared structure. Pell’s insistence on burial also changes the group’s relationship with the dead: the body cannot be treated only as a clue, obstacle, or contaminated object. Recorded alongside Carmen and the adventuring company; further relationships are not established here.
